As you see, [i]EA[/i] blessed ya boy with a review key when I asked. Did my stupendous writing woo them? The big follower count of my curator? 1018 hours in [i]FIFA 22[/i]? Perhaps my moustache? Yeah, it was probably the stache. It is pretty magnificent.

Before we start, the game finally comes equipped with an anti-cheat. But it's also a kernel-level anti-cheat. I'm aware of the debate surrounding this type of software, but I have no issue with it. I'm happy to share my homework folder with anyone, hacker or not.

But besides needing to install the anti-cheat software manually, I can't say I had any bugs or bees. Same for optimization. Running on a Ryzen 7 5800X paired with an RTX 3070 and 32GB of ram, all nicely displayed on my glorious ultrawide 1080p monitor with everything maxed out — it was all peachy.

[h2][b][i]The last dance[/i][/b][/h2]

First, let's talk gameplay. The meta shifts from short, fast, agile and lean players to just [b]lengthy[/b]. But what does lengthy mean? Well, it's a new style of sprinting, which determines what kind of running animations a player has. There is also explosive and controlled. But nobody cares about them — we all want to be lengthy. No use in lying. Yet only a select few meet the requirements - [b]high strength and low agility[/b]. Finally, players such as Lewandowski, van Dijk, Kane, Fabinho, Casemiro, etc., are usable. Seems EA liked the joke "[i]He runs like he has a third leg[/i]" so much they decided to make it a gameplay feature. And, oh boy! These lengthy men do be fast. They do need a couple of seconds to gain momentum tho and are still pretty poor in tight spaces. So, not stupidly overpowered like the previous meta. Ying-Yang boys, ying-yang. And I like how it has made "slower" defenders, below 85 pace, usable against pacey attackers, 90+ pace. This was something the ratty pace merchants would try and abuse, time and time again. How the turntables...

We also get a new type of shot — [b]the power shot[/b]. Finally, we can smash the ball as hard as possible. It does require manual aiming, so it's not as easy as the regular shot. But, please, [i]EA[/i], I'm begging you — do not make aiming semi-assisted in the future. Leave the risk-reward intact.

Another area that received some love is the set piece taking, giving us more control over how and where we hit the ball. Previously, only those using a keyboard could aim without the reticle spazzing like crazy. But now, you have a simple line showing where the ball will go and an indicator of the type of shot you'll take. It feels almost PES-like. However, I'm not a fan of not being able to zoom out during corners and free kicks like in previous entries. It makes set pieces in local co-op way harder to execute. I hope they bring the option back.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2869657264

And that's about it for the new stuff. Besides the abundance of new animations, courtesy of HyperMotion 2, and the continued refinement of player movement and physics, there is very little left to say. Perhaps nerfing the outside-the-foot shot? I've played games against people who do nothing but spam this shot type. It's just that overpowered.

But what about the modes the game offers?

Look, I'm gonna make this as quick and painless for you non-Ultimate Team players out there — yet again, almost nothing changed. [b]Pro Clubs[/b] is still the same 11v11 PvP it was all this time. [b]Volta[/b] again feels like a cheap Fifa Street populated only by selfish players. As for [b]Seasons[/b], it's just PvP with real-life clubs/nations. Can't really do much to improve that. But [b]Career mode[/b] did receive some new "stuff" — using real-life managers and a more interactive player career. The latter was fun, with your actions on and off the pitch pushing you towards one of the three personalities, each giving you different attribute boosts. Call your manager's mother a hamster, or buy a high-end mattress - the choice is yours!

With that out of the way, it's time to see what we, the gambling simulator addicts, get in this year's [i]FIFA Ultimate Team[/i], or FUT for short.

And what better way to start this segment than with a controversial take. So, lord, forgive me for the words I'm about to say — [b]FUT is live service done right.[/b]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2884903427

Alas, no, I'm not joking. To me, FUT is a perfect example of this model done right. It receives a healthy stream of content throughout the year; Special cards, daily SBCs, weekly objectives, multiple seasons with season passes to grind, player card objectives, and so on. I'm always incentivized to come back. And unlike the heavy Pay2Win pre-[i]FIFA 17[/i] era, being a non-paying customer and having a good team is completely viable now, with the game rewarding you for simply playing it.

And this year, we see tectonic changes to [b]the chemistry system[/b]. And boy, does me likey. Loyalty, the iconic green/yellow/red strings and penalties for low chemistry, like a fart in the wind, it's all gone. Instead, we have three squares to fill, with player stats not getting crucified due to low team or player chemistry. How is that possible? Magic probably. Best not to dwell on it. Instead, focus on how to fill them squares. Like before, players gain chemistry from nationality, league, and club links. But, now you need only worry about slotting the player in his god-given position so that he can give and receive chemistry.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2869576815

And I'm already in love with this change. The chemistry system of old felt restrictive, punishing me for trying to be creative if I didn't reach a certain chemistry threshold. Thankfully, now that is no longer the case, and [i]EA[/i] won't spank me for trying to use a unique team. Another new addition is [b]secondary positions[/b] for each player, which you can assign to them by using position modifiers on said player.

We also get more stuff to do with [b]FUT Moments[/b]. But I won't lie — it's pretty dull. Thrust into specific match scenarios, you're tasked with completing objectives - pass the ball 3 times, score a goal, don't concede, etc., all needing to be accomplished within a given timeframe. Not very creative, nor that interesting to do. But then again, you can only ask so much of players to do while playing a football match. And completing these objectives nets you stars, the mode's currency, which can be spent in its shop on some packs.

But for me, Squad Building Challenges, where you build squads and submit them to earn packs and players, are still the best part of FUT. They are like puzzles with unique requirements (only 5 players from one nation, no more than 3 leagues, squad rating 80, etc.) you must solve.

The rest...Well, Division Rivals and FUT Champs, the two main PvP modes,  see you duke it out with other players to see who is more sweaty and immature. As for Squad Battles...I would literally give EA money to remove it. The rewards are not that great for what is asked of you — play 40 games in a week and earn at least 1,5k points per match (World Class or higher difficulty) to reach Elite 1 (40-50k usually). Cut that number down to 20, and we can talk. The Draft is ok and has a PvP and offline version. But I think it's time for a change when you have an entry fee and crappy rewards. So, [i]EA[/i], just make it free. Allow people to enjoy one of the best aspects of FUT — making fun squads and using unique players.

So yeah, that's pretty much it, innit?

And with [i]EA[/i] closing the book on its [i]FIFA[/i] franchise by parting ways with [i]FIFA[/i] (the international governing body of football), it's truly the end of an era.

[b][i]FIFA[/i] is dead, long live [i]EA Sports FC![/i][/b]

This is a tough one for me to review, and a bit like football it is a game of two halves.

First half
Given the absolute and unmitigated cluster truck that was (and still is) the PC launch of Fifa 23, I completely understand the negative press and reviews it is getting and add my own dissenting voices to all the others on this subject.

I waited a few days after launch because of all the issues. It gave me an unrecoverable error. I briefly tried to resolve, before refunding.

It has to be said EA Support have absolutely no idea as to what they are doing. There were threads that were directed to Trello boards which in turn directed back to the forums, with requests for logs and very little information coming the other way. 

I decided for give it another go - after checking with Steam whether you could refund the same game twice, you can as long as it is within the usual refund parameters.

I read that Riva tuner could cause issues, so I simply disabled this. 

Without any real expectations that it would work, I re-installed it and it booted up. No errors (unrecoverable or otherwise), Anticheat installed ok (but appears to want to re-install on every boot of the game). It spent a fair while on the Loading screen until I found a firewall request hidden behind this, as soon as I enabled the firewall rule it booted straight into the menu. And this is where things turned.... interesting.

Second half
Ok, it was a terrible first half, by all rights there should be no coming back from it, but we have. I was expecting another own goal with performance issues, but I was very, very surprised!

I do have a beefy rig (5900x, 3090oc, super-fast SSD, 32gb etc) but the game runs flawlessly, I mean without a single stutter or frame issue and I am running it at 4k at constant 120hz (in game) and 60hz (replays) and it looks and feels AMAZING.

I have been a Fifa fan since the beginning, so feel in a position to be able to review objectively. This is the first Fifa that feels fluid. By that I mean the players react and do what you want them to do. 

It is possible to run at a defender and jink past them with a burst of speed - and it just feels natural.
I have none of the frustration where you dominate for 89 minutes, only to have the AI have one attempt in the last minute and score. It just feels perfectly balanced to me. I do think the difficulty has been reduced, I now play on professional (advising me to go to WC) - I have never been that good, hence it must be easier. 

That said, the game finally feels like football to me, you see a lot more out of the ordinary animations (rolls and falls etc) and much less stock animations - like the physics is finally working after all this time.

I could never time it right to score a volley pre-23, however in my first game I played in a wicked cross from the right wing and scored with a scissor kick - I almost passed out. 

The tutorial trainers are great, really gives you an insight of where the ball could go - whether in attack or defence.

Fifa has always been renowned for its presentation, however this time they have somehow improved on this too. You really feel you are watching a broadcast match. From the commentary, to the goal alerts, to the replays (which look SUBLIME now and like real replays), they flow in realtime from the play and back - truly dynamic and the way the ball flies though the air or skids along the ground is superb!

For my team (Chelsea) the player likenesses are outstanding (whilst not the same for all teams) - there are a few odd ones, but on the whole they are AMAZING. Stirling, Mount, Kepa, Kante, Aubameyang all look spot on. Even Graham Potter looks ok.

The intro to each match is liking watching Sky TV, and to hear your clubs anthems (and songs) ring out throughout the match is another class touch, but better implemented.

The crowd still has too many clones, however the way they surge towards you when you score at Stamford bridge, or do a Mexican wave in the open stadia of South America really adds to the authenticity.

The graphics truly are brilliant, the way the ball moves and interacts with the net is next gen. Hair moves – and Cucurella has a lot of it and it flows!!

Formations actually seem to make a difference. Set pieces now make much more sense, I have gone from never getting a shot on target in pre-23 to getting a shot on target once in 23!

The strength of players seems to be more apparent now too, so some off your beefier players can barge people off the ball, or hold up the ball better.

The Standing tackle has revolutionised defending. Get it right and you can turn defence into attack in an instant. In fact, every element of the game seems to be tweaked / updated, so the power meter for passes and shooting seems less random.

Sliding tackle is still a satisfyingly last-ditch affair if you are last man and need to stop someone quickly.

Offsides are less annoying than previously, and while Derek still never complains about a decision, he does comment that is must have been close!

The game never feels unfair, no longer will pinpoint accurate passes from the AI always reach their target, they are fallible. The game ebbs and flows at times, but it rewards patient build-up to the final third. If you take too long once you are there you can be severely punished by a well-timed counter attack – and the same goes both ways.

The amount of games modes caters for everyone, the introvert (Career), the extrovert (online), the introvert with extrovert tendencies (Volta) and trainspotters (FUT). This is not a dig by the way, some of my best friends are trainspotters!

The career is really feature packed and I love that you can turn things off (e.g. transfers etc) is great.

So, we are fast approaching full time, and given we ended the first half 6-0 down there was no way back, surely?

Well, in my honest opinion EA have outdone themselves with this game (notice I said game and not release).
 
Their Fifa swansong really is the best digital interpretation of Football I have ever played - and yes that includes pro-evo – which I will admit in some iterations felt more like football than Fifa, however that cannot be said anymore.

There are also more features I have not touched upon (Women’s football being one of them, Be a pro being another) as well as the World Cup updates that are due.

The thing is with a football game playing this well, with all these bells and whistles, have EA shot themselves in the foot. Without the Fifa license what will we lose when it turns to EA FC next year? They made a bold statement about Fifa holding them back, and it will be interesting to see if they are able to demonstrate that, but I worry they will need to take a few steps back next year before building on it again to get such a complete package. 

So, the final score? If we are factoring the launch and continuing issues, I’d give it a 2 and could not recommend it, however if you happen to be lucky like me and manage to actually get it work and work flawlessly then I would give it a perfect 10 – nothing has felt this much like football, since Match Day II with its revolutionary Diamond Deflection System – and nothing has impelled me to write such a long and rambling review of a computer game before, so that must be something right?

To top it all off I have got it working near flawlessly (at low res) on Steam deck so can take my progress with me! 

I highly recommend Fifa 23 – assuming you can get it to load and run flawlessly as mine does then I would go so far as to say Best. Sports. Game. Ever!!!

What a sublime end to the Fifa brand of football. 

If you can get over your frustration, your anger and your feeling of resentment towards a company that has no excuses for their bunged releases year on end, then I promise you this, you will end up smiling from ear to ear playing this years version.

I have been playing Fifa games since 1994 and there was a period in there for the last 5 or so years that Fifa just felt like it had been neglected, re-packaged, re-painted and re-gifted to us over and over. I will admit that last years version on console was a pretty great game but this one just feels so right.

For whatever reason I didn't suffer the anticheat issue, I started the game directly out of origin instead of steam and watched it bungle over itself a couple of times saying that the anticheat failed to load or some such rubbish before it just corrected itself and I never looked back.

8 hours in and I honeslty haven't been this motivated to play a fifa game in a decade. The visuals in this version, finally with hypermotion, looks fantastic. The changes to the pitch as you play, the stadiums, and the movement of players is amazing. The detail in the players themselves is incredible. I could never have imagined 28 years ago that a game of football on a computer screen (TV back then) could possibly look or play in such an amazing way. 

Yes we deserve for games to work in the way they are advertised. Yes a game should just load, its kind of fundamental to playing said game. No I have no idea how such a widespread error could make it to launch, particularly from a company as big as this one, and lets hope they understand the value of loyalty by offering some sort of in game compensation. Because we are the same people supporting their product year after year. 

But this is a review about the game you get to play once you overcome the ridiculous roadblocks so many are experiencing. With that in mind, the game is just fantastic. The commentary is the best its been, the sound is wonderful and the speed of the game makes it feel like you are truly playing a game of football. 

I hope so many of you will circle back around after you have played and consider adjusting your reviews to reflect the game, despite the terrible launch. Surely there are a huge team of people that truly poured their passion into delivering such a wonderful game and they must be devastated to have their work be completely overlooked and overshadowed by a poorly implemented anticheat software and a lack of real communication, action and support from their company to us their valued customers.

I hope you all get to experience this game soon and I am sorry for anyone who has been aching to play it, cleared their schedule, only to be faced with an issue that prevents that.

DISCLAIMER 1: I haven't owned or played a FIFA game since 1998 (PS1, Blur song :). I have no interest or intention of playing Ultimate team. I realize the game might be a hot buggy mess for many PC users- but I've had no issue, besides having to disable a controller setting in Steam and update my Nvidia drivers. 

DISCLAIMER 2: I'm American so I have very little exposure to the game of Futball. I might be able to name  half of the premier league teams, the powerhouse clubs of each major country, and a handful of the game's biggest stars. I'm a wannabe fan. I bought FIFA 23, despite all the terrible reviews for 3 reasons: 

1). World Cup is coming up and it's mostly the only Futball I ever watch- I love the event and thought the game would give me a primer.

2). I'm enjoying the hell out of the FX series, "Welcome to Wrexham." I've 100% bought in to the concept, history, and pride that comes with supporting a local club. Already started my Paul Mullin career.

3). Wrexham has given me the catalyst to finally pay attention to the Premier league and I'm excited to play out some matches, learn the teams, and stream(watch) some real games Saturday/Sunday Mornings. 

HONEST REVIEW:
Really enjoying the game- it mostly feels like the experience I remember from 20+ years ago. It's still a video game, so if you're a purist and expect a 100% translation of reality you'll probably get annoyed by the lack of anticipation and reactions of your fellow AI teammates, but that's all part of the game (why don't players follow up on my missed shots!). 

THE GOOD:
Career mode seems very cool. Again, haven't played in EA game in a long time, so maybe this is a tiresome feature, but I find it surprisingly deep and fun to play out (in various ways),

The Tutorial and Training games are excellent and I feel like I'm given the basics and the tools to hone my skills later. While the controls can be frustratingly precise it honestly feels like practice will be rewarded. 

The Graphics are quite good, as is the sound. The announcers will probably become tiresome, but I enjoy their banter.


THE BAD:
The Menus feel obtuse to me as a new player, especially as far as understanding the diverse game modes.

I haven't found a (tournament) mode that incorporates international teams (like a World Cup?). Maybe that's coming- seems like an oversight. I believe I can build my own custom tournament but that's a bit cumbersome for something so iconic to the sport. 

I can't comment on online play or ultimate team, neither have any interest for me personally. I understand that's a huge draw for the franchise, but there's too much content for a new FIFA owner to wade through I can't see myself bothering any time soon.

Origin, but whatever....


So if by any chance you're a player like me, getting a little gray around the temples, with a burgeoning interesting and appreciation for the beautiful game, little to no FIFA experience, I think you'll be pleasantly surprised with this title.

This is the best game ever. I really recommend it to you because everyone needs to see the audacity of EA who wants 60$ for this amazing football simulator. The game is worth 1500$ really. For just one game, you get 300 titles worth of bugs. Some games make you feel good while playing them. Well in FIFA 23, you feel useless because your players can't complete a simple pass while the opponents are superheroes. The game is full of many leagues around the world, but apparently nobody knows this since everybody online in seasons plays PSG. Prepare to have Mbappe's beautiful face engraved on your retina. Prepare to see countless moments of awkwardly bad skill moves performed by every opponent who woke up a Messi fan after seeing the World Cup this year. Playing online in higher divisions you'll have a blast, since most of the time it feels like the final result of a match is decided beforehand, and the game does what it needs to do to achieve that. This means unexplained passes/shots/failed tackles from your players and incredible shows of skill from not so highly rated opponent players. You'll miss 6 very easy shots and then the opponent will score a goal from outside the box to win the game. You'll see God himself as the ball will interpolate to the opponent driven by divine forces some smart guy at EA wrote in a late Friday night OT run. Your players will be unable to sprint (with 80% stamina available), unable to shoot, the game won't register your button presses (passes don't happen and shots go way over the goal after a simple button tap, etc), only to have your opponent get every ball and score a crappy goal after which he'll celebrate like he won the Champions League. During a match I conceded a corner goal because my goalkeeper didn't defend the goal and instead bugged out and kept looping a "yell at teammates" animation near the outer edge of the box. I filmed the moment and will show it to my kids so they know what failing in life means. But the fun times don't only happen in game. There were also many unexplained crashes (without any helpful error) on a system that otherwise runs very well. In the middle of the match, the game would just crash to desktop. Sometimes I think that even the game realizes what a failure it is and decides to terminate itself, but who knows? Oh, there's more good news - NO CHEATERS THIS YEAR! EA ANTICHEAT IS HERE TO SAVE US ALL. The pop up screen looks like an idiot who didn't learn about padding space designed it. It takes 20 seconds to load, and every single second feels like a waste of CPU cycles. Rest assured, the anticheat runs above your OS, so that any hacker who gets access to it can have a nice backdoor to your machine. But this won't happen since EA obviously is great at coding. There's also the joy of getting huge performance spikes whenever the game loads some higher model LODs. Let's just put it like this, optimization is probably one of the best ever seen by this industry. Cyberpunk has a lot to learn from this game. I would be very proud to launch such a product and claim upwards of 60$ for it, especially given that it's pretty much just a reskin of FIFA 17/18/19/20/21/22 with some useless features added on top.  Hypermotion 2000 v3 or however it's called is the best feature in gaming history. I absolutely love seeing replays of marvelous broken gameplay moments with some extra lame graphics overlaid on top of them while me and the opponent behind the replay furiously mash the skip button. The only thing I'm sad about is that I didn't get the opportunity to spend more on this beautiful FoOtBalL sImUlAtOr, but I didn't get into FUT yet, and that's what FUT is for, isn't it? I totally reccomend this game!

I have played quite a few hours now, and think I have a better idea for this review. I wanted to feel like my time in career is worth it but after hours of career, it feels like they don't care how well I play. 

You start the career with any team (even the best team) and work to make it as a starter... and that's the game. Once you are a starter it feels like there is nothing else to do that is fun. You don't have a room to check out your trophies you win, you can't spend money on anything like a new outfit or a bigger house, or even maybe things inside the house. Purchasing an investment that is just some lines of text feels incredibly boring. 
I think having a story-line, for instance starting on a low end team and working up to the best team is a cool goal to strive for. Having cool cut scenes and stuff as you achieve an end goal makes it exciting to accomplish. Right now it feels like there is nothing to accomplish unless you make your own situation up. 

The game focuses heavily on playing as a manager or playing as someone else, they focus very little on the rp aspect and it means people who enjoy the campaign have little to look forward to. Every year I find myself watching videos, hoping that they implement more to make it feel rewarding to play the campaign and was hoping this would be the one... 
It was not the one.

The soccer mechanics work incredibly well, I found the game to consist of very few bugs. The main menu is poorly optimized so even on my 4080 it seems to lag a little. It's quite satisfying to score goals and if you simply want to just play virtual soccer, this version is the best one yet. Hopefully they add some love to the campaign to spruce it up for all the people who want a more story driven campaign.

If I trace back when I actually started to play Football video games, It was with the mid 90's. But Football games changed a lot at some point so I'd say the real start was around 2005 with Winning Eleven. I was really into it, learning all the tricks and details and always trying to play how it is played in real life (which doesn't necessarily works in video games btw). Anyway, I had a lot of fun especially with Career modes (Master League it was called). I played mostly the Konami Franchise since, but every now and again I played Fifa. 

I stopped a couple of years ago and been just playing Football games once in a while so my feedback is not from a serious competitive Fifa gamer. It is from someone who just want some fun and don't play serious online matches. 

So, in terms of fun for sure it is one of the best Football games I played. I know that people are hating the game because of the pay to win system of FUT and loads of other things compared to recent Fifa games I understand. But I am enjoying the game as someone who used to be a fanatic and now just want to have fun.

One of the things that people complain a lot is about unrealistic animations like the player skidding or sliding to reach a ball as if he is on skates etc. I used to agree with that. But on a second thought I realized that if in one hand it is very unrealistic compared to the Konami game (which changes name all the time) now Efootball on the other hand it is more fluid. I used to be a puritan towards realism in a football game, but at the end of the day it is a video game want it or not and being a real simulator can start to crash with the reality that it is not more than a toy on a screen with a controller. In other words, when I compared to the Efootball series, Fifa really felt more fluid (my past self would be mad reading this) but like I said, at the end of the day, it is a game and I support some adjustments to make it feel more fluid and more like a enjoyable game rather than a clumsy controlling of dummies. It is how Efootball felt after playing fifa for a while (I was a Konami franchise fanatic for decades). 

Other than that , the fact that you have licenses for all the teams and many controlling tweaks is a good plus compared to Efootball.

What I really disgust in this game is that the trainning options are basically none. You can't train set pieces properly. You can't have a classic training game like in older games. All you have is a player vs goalkeeper scenario, that sucks.

Low crosses are a bit awkard and they sometimes go too weak.

Scoring headers on crosses are way less efficient than in many other games I played. 

I love scoring headers but it seems like it is very hard on this game.

The game is fun but lacks some essential small things like trainning. The online mode I am not commenting about because It's not my focus.

Edit - 1 week later, and still no fixes in sight. Getting less than 10 fps on a high end system. Sticking to Fifa 22 for now. 


First impressions review.

They really need a maybe recommend option cause this is really a not today, but soon kind of recommend. It's breaking ground in terms of being able to both go forward in terms of graphics quality while at the same time going backwards in terms of quantity. What I mean is that it's poorly optimised perhaps, or for whatever reason you can run a smooth 60 fps (top cap though you can choose unlimited) and it will run that perfectly, until it doesn't. Then you are playing a new form of turn based FIFA and your opponent gets 1 free turn and is always ahead of you. 

Now I say better quality because the players out of the gate, and these are the noname FUT bois I get in the starter packs look amazing. It looks like they do simple gfx when you are playing the match, but then load up the high res when you zoom in on the moments, like the celebrations. I'm fine with that. I don't need to see what Son's hair is doing from 200 meters out, but it's a nice touch when you land a stellar goal and the team is going mental! 

Hyper motion is it? It's fine. It's just a slightly better after goal cam occasionally, with some token info that flashes up too fast to process. In time I'll find out what it means but for now it mostly just downgrades the performance. 

Ok, lastly thing I like most about FIFA 23 over Fifa 22? 

The physics seem to have changed and NGL, I absolutely love watching my ST eat Sh*t when he misses his hand off and fully faceplants / flys over the keeper. The ragdoll might have changed or something but I crack up every time, and that's coming off the back of a full year playing Fifia 22. I cannot not recommend highly enough choosing the Womens team as you entry match that the game STILL forces you to play on your first load of the game. You will see dudes running around for the whole next year. Let this be that one glorious time to see you ST go flying into the net, which they now hit if you get the angle right. And that angle can be triangle now. 

The thing I like the least from 22? 

SAME DAMNED ANNOUNCERS!? WTF? Get some new lines. I mostly bought this cause I was hoping to NOT have the exact same BS calls anymore. They were fine but I already heard Derek Rae and Co for over a year. Time to move the fuck on. And it costs so little and adds soo much to the game atmosphere. Huge miss here for me. If you played 22 you heard it all before and it is exactly the same sound file. Zero work was done here on a multi billion dollar game. It's so fuc|<3n weak. 

Do I recommend right now? 

Nah. I recommend you update your drivers and give it a week. Then update them again and learn how to "Clear (your) Directx shader cache"

Also I'll add the play feels slow but that's most likely coming from my All 100 stat man team at the end of 22, into a 80 rated team of noobs. Slow is fine to get a feel for the game, but it mostly feels the same. The controls are mostly the same. Corner kicks have changed, and not sure yet how to feel about that as I usually just play them short. It has potential but it's also the time when the game sh[ts the bed and turns into a 10 fps slog the most often. Corners aren't the only time the slowdowns happen but they are so far the most common for me. As the saying goes, they will fix this in time but for $120 this should be good to go on day one and it's not and it's their laziness of waiting for the problem rather than hunting it down, that caused this. 

TLDR;  GFX up, Performence down, wait a week.

EA, you did it again. You messed up the launch, again. Like you do every year. It is totally unacceptable that you charge almost 100 bucks for the Ultimate Edition that grants you 3 days early access - let us be real, that is why most of us buy Ultimate Edition - but launching the game 3 days early is basically a game of Russian roulette - either you are lucky as hell and the game launches and plays, or you are unlucky like thousands of consumers and get error messages, failing anti-cheat and whatever else there is preventing people from getting what they paid for. This is a complete slap in the face to your customers and something you should address immediately. 

The anti-cheat is a good idea and I am glad it is coming to PC, as the previous iterations of FIFA on PC were clearly plagued by hackers - so this is a welcomed addition, but the execution of the anti-cheat is horrendous. I know people that bought the Ultimate Edition that should have been able to play the game 2 days ago that still can not launch the game due to the anti-cheat being absolutely garbage. Fix this. 

Bugs, where do I begin? There are a plethora of bugs in the game, from missing sponsors on a dozen of kits, visual bugs like the ball becoming super blurry and the performance of the actual game itself completely tanking. I am on a 3060 and an i5-11400CPU and there is no chance in hell my FIFA should be full of stutters and lags. The lag in the menu is atrocious, set-pieces and cinematics (I love the addition of cinematics) is PLAGUED by frame-drops which makes them horrible and painful to look at. Given how much of a copy-paste game FIFA is every year, these bugs are inexcusable. 

Usually, every year, we are used to getting the new stadiums of the teams that are promoted to say the Premier League. Where is Nottingham Forest' stadium? Last year you had to give us Leeds' stadium through an update later and you were excused due to COVID, but what is the excuse now? This is just laziness - you mean to tell me a billion dollar company like EA with well over a year of development can not make the stadium ready for release? Call this nitpicking, but for me it is the small things that matter.

As far as actual gameplay goes, I do enjoy the feeling of the players and the ball. It feels like the players and the ball have actual weight to it now and it feels much less arcade-like to me. I thoroughly enjoy the slower pace feel, although it could do with some fine tuning. The new engine makes a massive difference (thank God you brought it to PC this year) and it is noticeable, so in that regard I am hopeful for a good year of FIFA. 

With all of these things addressed, I would like to say this year sees the end of an era. I started playing FIFA in 2003 on my brother's original Xbox and I have played pretty much every iteration since. I grew up with the game and I have so many good memories like coming home from school and inviting friends over to play some FIFA. That is what the beautiful game is all about - the game that has seen us cry, laugh, angry and every other conceivable emotion possible. The game we know as "FIFA" will be no more, but that does not mean the end of football games - I am hopeful for the future and I HOPE that EA will start caring more and focus on improving their games and game-modes that have been heavily neglected (I am looking at you, Career Mode and Pro Clubs). 

Arrivederci, FIFA, it has been an honour.
